target_customer: Muslim parents with children aged 1 to 12 who pay a monthly subscription for Islamic-values cartoons
problem: Muslim parents struggle to find high quality children's content that matches their values, and algorithms on open platforms push unsuitable content.
business_model: Consumer subscription streaming (7.99 USD per month at launch per press release) plus planned merchandise and games
product_category: Islamic children's streaming platform and animation studio

founders.name: Sinan Ismail
prior_employers: Digital Durian (co-founded animation studio behind Didi & Friends and Omar & Hana)
education: Mathematics, Universiti Sains Malaysia (per Digital News Asia)
previous_startups: Digital Durian (animation house; he still owns it, cash flow was tight)
founders.background_notes: Digital Durian co-founder is Hairul Faizal Izwan; not recorded as a Durioo founder.

competitors.name: Muslim Kids TV
competitors.what: Subscription app with Islamic videos, channels, games, cartoons and songs from Milo Productions
competitors.traction_then: unknown; undated third-party estimate of about 98K installs

competitors.name: Miraj
competitors.what: Free ad-free app with Islamic stories, Quran learning, games and animations for ages 4 to 9

technical_complexity.rationale: A streaming app and content library; the hard part was producing original animation at quality, which the founders had done for 13 years at Digital Durian.

defensibility.rationale: Owned original characters and a content library with known creators are hard to copy; the app itself is easy. About 45 creators moved from Digital Durian in January 2022.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent response found; the founder said YouTube's 2020 child-content policy changes cut Digital Durian revenue by up to 70 percent, which motivated owning the platform.

market_need_then: Digital News Asia reports the founder's claim of 70 million Muslim families online, YouTube monetization changes for kids' content in 2020, and about 22,000 paid subscribers by early 2023, 99 percent in Malaysia.

identity.mascot_or_character: Characters from Omar & Hana and Didi & Friends; Goldbeak movie pack (press listing)

branding.brand_signature: Creators of Omar & Hana and Didi & Friends, with billions of YouTube views
branding.community_and_virality: Parent studio claims about 6 to 8 billion cumulative YouTube views and 7 million subscribers, which seeded the audience.

brand_strength.rationale: Inherited a large existing audience and recognizable characters; the Durioo name itself is new and unexplained.

outcome_analysis: Durioo moved a content studio with a large YouTube audience into its own subscription app, joined YC in Winter 2022 and raised a 2.85M USD seed announced in March 2023 with about 22,000 paid subscribers. It is active with about 50 to 65 staff. Later subscriber or revenue data were not found, so the long run outcome is unknown, but owned characters and an inherited audience were clear strengths.
notes: Company site returned HTTP 503 so was not read. Seed was closed by October 2022 and announced 2023-03-01. CB Insights reports 3.35M total over 3 rounds and Bouncewatch reports 12.5M, both conflicting aggregators, not recorded. A pre-seed of undisclosed amount is mentioned in press (not recorded as a round). YC description says 3 billion views for one cartoon while the YC bio says 8 billion across two. Competitor app store listings are undated and were not available as dated sources; they are included with the date null. Direct competition from free YouTube channels is not recorded as a named competitor.
